title: Colossians: complete in Christ

lines: Colossians was written from prison to a small church Paul had never seen. Epaphras, one of its own people, had carried the gospel home.
Now some teaching promised more: visions, food rules, holy days, and attention to angels and powers.

scripture.text: You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant

lines: The first two chapters are about who Christ is, and the last two about how believers live. The turn comes at the start of chapter three.
The commands of the second half grow out of the gifts of the first.

scripture.text: since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the song of Christ
lines: Christ is the image of the invisible God. All things were made through him and for him.
He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
Firstborn means the heir with first place, not the first thing made, as the church confessed at Nicaea.

scripture.text: He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.

lines: All the fullness of God dwells in Christ, and believers are complete in him.
Israel's feasts and Sabbaths were good gifts, a shadow pointing ahead, not a lie. The powers people feared were disarmed at the cross.

scripture.text: These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.

lines: Believers put off the old self, with its anger, greed, and lies. They put on compassion, kindness, patience, and forgiveness.
And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
In the renewed self there is no Greek or Jew, slave or free. Christ is all.

scripture.text: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.

lines: Paul puts every relationship in the Lord. He speaks to the weaker first, and lays duties, not privileges, on the stronger.

Churches read the words to wives and husbands differently. All agree they give no one a license to control or harm another, and nothing in them asks anyone to stay where they or their children are in danger.
The words to slaves were misused for centuries to defend slavery. That misuse was wrong.

scripture.text: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men

lines: Christians differ on who wrote the letter. Paul himself, as the letter says and the early church received it. A follower of Paul after his death, as many scholars since the eighteen hundreds have argued. Or Timothy during Paul's life, with his approval.
This film takes no side.
Read it in one sitting, aloud if you can. Then read the song of Christ slowly, more than once.
Let it ask whether you have treated Christ as a good beginning, and looked elsewhere for the rest.
And you have been made complete in Christ.

scripture.text: And you have been made complete in Christ
